headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane’s file uploads and broad egress can leak Marker-processed document content, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks stay low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem, network, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest Plane output automatically. Plane can accept file uploads, but there is no documented shared channel or parser bridge. Any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Plane text into Marker prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside these profiles, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Plane content into Marker prompts.
Strip instructions from uploaded files before review.
Use a human review step for any text transferred between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane exposes file uploads and broad network egress, so document content processed by Marker can flow into Plane if transferred. Marker itself has no network egress and no filesystem read/write, which limits direct exfiltration, but the shared document workflow still creates a default leakage path for files and notes. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Marker outputs sensitive document text into Plane uploads or notes, that content is exposed to Plane's backend.
IF both agents are used on the same confidential files, leakage risk is present in the default workflow.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive Marker outputs into Plane.
Redact secrets before transferring documents.
Use separate tenants or workspaces for confidential material.
Disable or restrict file uploads in Plane where possible.
Review retention settings for uploaded files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while Plane also lacks filesystem write and only advertises broad egress plus file uploads. There is no overlapping mutable resource or lock-free write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory, this assessment no longer holds.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable state, conflict risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared artifacts.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Use separate project folders for each agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can consume files and notes, so Marker’s document-processing output may become Plane input without a documented verification step. That creates a plausible cascade where extracted facts or summaries are treated as authoritative. Marker is not action-taking, but Plane can operationalize the content into tasks and scheduling workflows, so the downstream impact is broader than a single document.
conditions: IF Marker output is imported into Plane without human verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Plane users create tasks from Marker summaries, downstream actions may reflect extraction mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review before importing Marker output into Plane.
Attach source documents to Plane tasks for verification.
Mark extracted text as untrusted until checked.
Use a checklist for fact validation before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is Plane’s file-upload and external API surfaces versus Marker’s local document-processing posture, which can create policy gaps if sensitive documents are moved between them. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair’s data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF Marker processes data subject to deletion/export obligations and Plane stores copies, compliance handling becomes relevant.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for Plane uploads.
Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Document a deletion/export process for uploaded files.
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated data.
